current_flow: The wiring already emits deleteMessageId for retire/allowed and replaceMessageId otherwise (job-permission-wiring-setup.ts:391). Slack's delivery handles replaceMessageId via chat.update and ignores deleteMessageId, so an allowed retire falls through to a new generic send (slack/channel-delivery.ts:104); Discord edits via messageMutations.edit and likewise ignores deleteMessageId (discord/index.ts:184); Teams sends zero-action retire/replace messages through sendTeamsTextMessage and handles neither option (teams/progress.ts:44). Only Telegram returns jobPermissionCardRetireDelivery (domain/types.ts:601). Chat prompts already delete (Slack response_url delete_original, Discord DELETE then PATCH receipt) or update the Adaptive Card to a receipt (Teams interaction-handlers.ts:423).

criteria_map.when every row of a job permission card: steps 1-4: shared settlement helper (persisted-marker short-circuit + same-message lane) hoisted from Telegram; Slack chat.delete then chat.update receipt; Discord DELETE then PATCH receipt via the rate-limited mutation requester; Teams updateAdaptiveCard receipt card or plain receipt when no activity id; all return jobPermissionCardRetireDelivery.
criteria_map.expired retire revisions reach Slack, Di: steps 2-4: expired retire keeps the replace path (chat.update / PATCH / updateAdaptiveCard with 'Expired: <command>' lines); step 5 keeps the retire-delivery result shape; the reconciler records deletedAt/receiptMessageId/deleteFailedAt as in T1.
criteria_map.existing unit and Postgres integration s: step 7: channels + application unit suites, tsc, check:architecture; Postgres permission-decision-chain lane host-side stays 5/5.
